sections.overview: The Common Pochard is a migratory diving duck widespread across Eurasian wetlands. It shares the genus Aythya with the Greater Scaup (Aythya marila). Unlike this relative, it chiefly uses vegetated inland waters.
sections.identification: In breeding plumage, the male has a chestnut head, black breast and pale grey body, while the female is browner.
sections.habitat: It breeds on vegetated freshwater lakes and ponds, then winters on larger freshwater or brackish waters.
sections.diet: Diving birds gather aquatic seeds, roots and leaves, as well as molluscs, crustaceans, worms and insect larvae.
sections.behavior: It migrates between northern and eastern breeding areas and more southerly wintering wetlands, often joining mixed duck flocks.
sections.reproduction: The female nests in waterside vegetation and incubates the clutch alone; the male generally leaves after laying.
sections.ecology: Its dependence on productive wetlands links its fortunes to the condition of freshwater habitats along its migratory route.
sections.conservation: The global assessment lists it as Vulnerable with a decreasing population; wetland loss, hunting and pollution are reported pressures.
